findings.text: The decorator skips generating `__rich_repr__` whenever `hasattr(cls, '__rich_repr__')` is true, and that includes methods inherited from a decorated parent. A subclass such as `@auto(angular=True) class B(A)` therefore never gets its `angular` flag applied, so it keeps the parent's setting. The parent's auto-generated `__rich_repr__` is reused and reads `inspect.signature(self.__init__)` of the subclass. Attributes that `B.__init__` takes but doesn't store make `repr()` raise `ReprError`.
